    Section 5: Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 5.4 #

    Proposition 5.2: over a brick-finite string algebra every nonsimple brick has a brick submodule or quotient of dimension one less (string_hasSmallerBrick). Theorem 5.4 (specialBiserial_hasSmallerBrick): the same over a brick-finite special biserial algebra, given by path data.

    source
    theorem BrickAccessibility.isSimpleModule_quot_iff {A : Type u} [Ring A] {I : Ideal A} [I.IsTwoSided] {M : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module (A ⧸ I) M] [IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ I) M] :
    IsSimpleModule (A ⧸ I) M ↔ IsSimpleModule A M

    A module on which A acts through A ⧸ I is simple over A ⧸ I exactly when it is simple over A.

    theorem BrickAccessibility.exists_submodule_finrank_one {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type u} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {Q : Statement.FinQuiver} (D : PathData Q A) (hspan : Submodule.span k (Set.range fun (p : Q.V × List Q.A) => D.pval p.1 p.2) = ⊤) (hadm : D.IsAdmissible) (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module k M] [IsScalarTower k A M] [FiniteDimensional k M] [Nontrivial M] :
    ∃ (L : Submodule A M), Module.finrank k ↥L = 1

    A nonzero finite-dimensional module over an algebra with admissible path data has a one-dimensional submodule.
